newsitem.title: USA: OfficeMax to buy Staples, Office Depot stores.
newsitem.headline: OfficeMax to buy Staples, Office Depot stores.

text.p: After round-the-clock negotiations, OfficeMax agreed Wednesday to help clear the way for Staples and Office Depot to gain government approval of their $4 billion merger by acquiring 63 of their stationary superstores.

The Federal Trade Commission, which rejected the merger on Monday and has been preparing to go to federal court to seek an injunction against the deal between the rival office supply chains, quickly issued a statement that said, "If they have something serious to talk about we will talk."

OfficeMax announced that it agreed to purchase 28 Office Depot office superstores and 35 Staples superstores, located from Washington State to Washington D.C., for $108.75 million. OfficeMax said it expected the stores to start making money for it as soon as the deal goes through.

"This was the culmination of three days of around-the-clock negotiations," OfficeMax Chief Executive Michael Feuer said in an interview from the company's Cleveland headquarters. "It became apparent it had to be a win-win-win deal for the three companies."
Staples Inc. Chairman Tom Stemberg said OfficeMax Inc. is getting "bargain basement" prices for the stores. He said the 63 stores "are doing business at a rate of about $6 million a year.
"Typically stores like that are sold for between $3 million and $4 million (each). We are selling for 1-3/4 million," he said.
"So I am not jumping up and down about the price. However, in the greater scheme of things, it was acceptable," he said after a presentation at a Merrill Lynch retailing conference.
Experts said the agreement may provide the needed breakthrough to win government approval of the deal.
The FTC voted 4-1 Monday to go to Federal District Court to block the merger, arguing that it would raise prices to consumers.

FTC Commissioner Mary Azcuenaga, the sole dissenter, declined to discuss the Staples-Office Depot case. But in a brief interview Wednesday, she noted that after the commission votes to go to court, "often the parties are talking to try to reach a settlement."

Richard Steuer, an antitrust expert with Kaye, Scholer in New York, said he believed the FTC would now approve the deal. "The agencies really have expressed the desire to be very flexible and to search for solutions," he said. "They do not see their role to be obstructionist."

But a former senior official of the FTC now in private practice, Kevin Arquit of Rogers & Wells in New York, was far more cautious. He said that although the deal seemed to settle FTC concerns, "I think strategically the companies were very ill-advised to wait until the last minute."

He said once the FTC gets ready to go to court "the dynamics change." Arquit pointed out that last-minute efforts to settle failed for drugstore chains Rite-Aid and Revco last year, after the FTC started proceedings againstg them.

Sources close to the talks between the government and Office Depot and Staples, which mostly took place at staff level, said the FTC had been willing to settle the case if OfficeMax purchased 62 stores.
But OfficeMax turned down that offer because the price was too high and the stores were not strong enough.
Feuer said the deal makes OfficeMax truly a national company, giving it 18 stores in the Washington-Baltimore area and 14 additional stores in the Los Angeles area.
"We had 19 in Los Angeles and plans to add 20 more this year," he said. "So now we'll fly by the 50 mark."
Feuer said this means the two new chains would be competitive everywhere. He said the mix of stores was far better than the original offer.
The negotiations became increasingly more tense as time passed, according to those close to the talks.

At 6 p.m. Tuesday the talks broke down, even though the mix of stores had been largely agreed upon, because of a $70 million disagreement. But the two sides came together again and managed to cut a deal.
At one point, Feuer said, he received threats from people who had lost money when the deal appeared to collapse Monday and blamed OfficeMax. A 24-hour armed guard was hired to protect him.

"It was getting a little scary with a lot of nasty calls because we were viewed as the spoiler," Feuer said. He said that when he was giving a speech Tuesday evening, a balloon popped and his guard pulled his gun.
If the combination of Staples and Office Depot does go through, some believe it will be a loss to consumers.
James Love, of the Ralph Nader-headed Centre for Responsive Law in Washington, said he believed that if the FTC approved the merger it would mean higher prices for consumers.
OfficeMax stock rose $1.75 to $15 and Office Depot jumped $3.75 to $23.125, both on the New York Stock Exchange, while Staples fell $1.25 to $22 on Nasdaq.
